title: U.S. citizen returning to the United States
facts: U.S. citizens traveling internationally generally should use a valid U.S. passport or other document specifically authorized for the mode and route of travel when entering the United States.
U.S. citizens, including dual nationals, are generally expected under federal law to use a U.S. passport to enter and leave the United States, subject to statutory and regulatory exceptions.
Airline boarding-document requirements can prevent travel even where citizenship itself is not in doubt.
Land and sea travel can have document options that differ from international air travel.
